cross_references.relationship: sibling — traditional mandamus for ministerial duties. §1085 compels an official to do what the law requires. §1094.5 reviews whether an agency abused its discretion in a decision after a hearing. Different tools for different problems.

procedural foundation — the Administrative Procedure Act (Gov. Code §§11500+) governs the hearings that produce the administrative decisions reviewed under §1094.5. The APA sets the hearing rules; §1094.5 sets the judicial review rules.
cross_references.build_status: NOT BUILT AS STANDALONE STANDARD — Cal. APA (Gov. Code §§11500+) procedural context documented within ccp_1094_5 reasoning layer.

cross_references.relationship: framework sibling — Government Claims Act. When an administrative agency decision causes harm, the question of whether the entity is liable in tort is governed by the Claims Act (§§810-996.6). §1094.5 reviews the decision; the Claims Act governs liability for damages.

federal alternative — when a state agency decision violates federal constitutional rights, §1983 provides a federal cause of action. The exhaustion of state remedies (including §1094.5) is NOT required before filing a §1983 claim (Patsy v. Board of Regents, 457 U.S. 496 (1982)).
